assessment.overall_rationale: This is a strong baseline replicate: modules 1 and 2 are near-identical restatements of the same detoxification and lipid-catabolism gene programs, module 3 shares the same Cdo1-centered sulfur/nitrogen disposal core with added refinements in the right replicate, and cross-pairs show only weak, mechanistically unrelated gene/regulator overlaps.

pair_scores.rationale: Nearly identical Phase I/II detoxification gene sets (Sult2a5/7/8, Gsta3, Akr1c6, Aldh1a1, Cyp2c50) with the same bile acid/steroid conjugation-excretion mechanism and shared Tpst1 regulator.
Shares only the aldehyde-clearing gene Aldh3a2 but the core mechanisms differ sharply: conjugation/excretion detoxification versus peroxisomal fatty acid beta-oxidation.
Both are hepatocyte metabolic programs sharing the Insig1 regulator, but xenobiotic/steroid detoxification and cysteine/taurine catabolism are unrelated core mechanisms.
Shares the Cyb5b gene and Abcg5 regulator, but lipid droplet/peroxisomal fatty acid handling is mechanistically distinct from Phase I/II xenobiotic-steroid conjugation.
Nearly identical gene sets (Fitm1, Hao2, Eci2, Aldh3a2, Lonp2) and Dgat2 regulator describe the same peroxisomal/ER fatty acid catabolism and lipid droplet biogenesis mechanism.
Shares only the Sord gene; peroxisomal lipid oxidation and sulfur amino acid/taurine catabolism are unrelated core processes.
Minimal gene/regulator overlap and no shared mechanism between nitrogen/sulfur amino acid disposal and xenobiotic Phase I/II detoxification.
No meaningful gene or mechanistic overlap between urea-cycle/sulfur amino acid catabolism and peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation.

Both center on Cdo1-driven cysteine-to-taurine catabolism feeding urea/polyamine disposal (Agmat, Car5a) with shared G6pc/Insr regulators, while the right module adds an aging (Rgn) and glucose-homeostasis refinement.
